ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, $DE \perp AB$, $\cos A = \frac{3}{5}$, and $AE = 6$, then what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ADE$ is a right-angled triangle,\\
hence $DA=\frac{AE}{\cos A}=6\times \frac{5}{3}=10$,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
it follows that AB=AD=10,\\
thus, the answer is: AB=\boxed{10}.
